# Centralization of a group generated by its root subgroups

This internal construction extends centralization from a split maximal
torus to the entire semisimple group under explicit root-generation and
vector-line hypotheses. Its ambient consequence uses the original
normalized-conjugation action and gives an actual map into any supplied
representative of the full centralizer. All results hold at every universe
over any algebraically closed field, without a characteristic restriction.

Let `H` be semisimple over `k`, let `s : S.toGrp ⟶ H` be a split maximal
torus, and assume `SemisimpleRootGenerationStatement` at the same universe.
For an actual action `b : AutomorphicAction K H` with `K` affine,
`AutomorphicAction.fixedSubgroup_eq_top_of_rootGeneration` assumes that each
intrinsic root functor for `s` lies in `b.fixedSubgroup`. The published
field fixed-subgroup theorem supplies a closed representative `c : C ⟶ H`.
Every root functor lies in `range c`, so the root-generation premise makes
`range c` the full subgroup functor. Its representing equality then proves
`b.fixedSubgroup = ⊤`. This uses generation among closed subgroups rather
than an assertion about finite products of points on arbitrary tests.

For `AutomorphicAction.eq_trivial_of_rootGeneration_vectorLines`, the
acting group `K` is explicitly a vector group of dimension one, the action
fixes the image of `s` on every test, and every intrinsic root functor for
`s` has a supplied representative that is a vector group of dimension one.
The published induced-root-action theorem and vector-line rigidity put
each root functor in the full fixed subgroup. The preceding closed
generation argument then proves that the action is the actual trivial
action, by testing each point with the identity refinement.

In the ambient situation take `h : H ⟶ G` monic and `a : K ⟶ G`, with
`range h` normalized by `range a`. Assume `range a` centralizes the image
of `s ≫ h`, and retain semisimplicity of `H`, split maximality of `s`,
root generation, and both vector-line premises just described.
`range_le_centralizer_of_rootGeneration_vectorLines` applies the action
theorem to `ofNormalizedConjugation h a hn`. The torus-fixedness lemma
supplies its fixed-map premise. The ambient conjugation formula, now with
trivial action, says that `a(q)` commutes with `h(x)` for every pair of
points. Reversing that commutation gives precisely
`range a ≤ (AutomorphicAction.conjugation h).fixedSubgroup`, including
every test scheme and every refinement.

If `a` is also monic and `c : C ⟶ G` represents this full centralizer,
`rootGeneratedCentralizerLift` constructs an actual homomorphism `K ⟶ C`
from inclusion of the represented subgroup functors.
`rootGeneratedCentralizerLift_comp` proves that its composite with `c`
is the original map `a`. No closedness, smoothness, or finite-type
assumption on the supplied centralizer representative is needed.

The provenance is the internal combination of field fixed-subgroup
representability, the explicit semisimple root-generation premise,
induced actions on represented root subgroups, vector-line rigidity,
and the natural lifting theorem for represented subgroup functors.
This construction does not establish the root-generation premise,
dimension-one vector structure for reductive root groups, a compatible
maximal torus in a given normal subgroup, or semisimplicity of that
normal subgroup. Consequently it does not prove the unconditional
normal-root dichotomy or the host almost-simple-generation statement.
